question: Under matched camera, contact, mission and spawn conditions, does the revised RGB action algorithm complete both physical deliveries faster and more reliably than frozen v26 RGB, and can a newly trained ACT control loaded beam motion without false arrival or loss of contact?
research_scope: Local saved-plan component study. It does not measure new LLM communication, map generalization, real robot performance, or ACT benefit from a matched old checkpoint unless that comparator is added in a separately frozen cohort.

known_durations_wall_s.v26_repeat_failure: TOP box tracking ambiguity before release; the 199.144 s is not a successful completion time
known_durations_wall_s.interpretation: The recent approximately 200 s RGB times are open/seed11 saved-plan runs; older ACT timings used a different synchronous controller/runtime. They guide run budgets but are not a matched speed comparison.

fixed_inputs.route_overlap: --auto-route-overlap --overlap-start grasp; verify selected independent open routes and shared apron exclusion in each result
fixed_inputs.camera_and_actor_boundary: Original own fixed RGB and common fixed TOP RGB, authored static map and own issued commands. No referee coordinates/contact/joints used by control.
fixed_inputs.model_and_data_freeze: Record source commit/tree, execution bundle ID/hash, Python/package versions, grasp/stage/ACT model hashes, exact scene XML/config/plan hashes and raw input/output hashes before comparing arms. No model retraining, source edits or case selection after first physical outcome.

cli_contract.per_trial_flags: Supply a fresh --output, the case's three --spawn-offset numbers, and the arm's --max-wall-s. ACT adds --carry-act-model MODEL_DIR --carry-act-python /Users/changmin/Project-Runtimes/ugrp/.venv-reference-act/bin/python --carry-act-stop-mode rgb_guarded; RGB omits all ACT flags. The dispatch launcher inserts --executor skills itself and forwards unrecognized options to run_dispatch_e2e.
cli_contract.unsupported_flags: At design checkout 41a906c, --episode-config and --carry-policy are not CLI inputs. carry_policy is an output result field. New CLI support is not assumed.

case_selection.candidate_training_split_as_reported_by_: Nine full training episodes: older F1/F2/F5/F6 plus realtime v19 four runs and v25-full. Four development episodes: older F3/F4 (kept together because they share image SHA values), realtime v25-repeat and v26-full. The training owner reports zero train/development image-SHA overlap; audit final dataset manifest before executing. Older missing-image dev-open/dev-turn are excluded. These are checkpoint-selection data, not physical test cases.
existing_exposed_conditions: The seven successful real-time ACT training/development source runs are open/seed11/original spawn and stored plan. Older F-series episodes add exposed scene families to train/development. Whole-episode and zero-image-SHA split does not make the development cases independent physical holdout.

2026-09-22 parallel ACT tests [-0.015,0.008,0], [0.015,-0.008,0], [0,0,1] and research-controller qualification [-0.010,0.004,-0.5], [0.008,-0.004,0.5], [0.020,0.003,-1.0] were inspected and are regression cases.
The previous screening also used [0.012,-0.006,0] on open and [-0.012,0.006,0] on shared_crossing.
case_selection.selection_audit: Both exact offset triples were absent from the inspected 2026-09-22 parallel-transport, parallel-act-study, research-controller-qualification, 2026-09-23 realtime-dispatch, and 2026-09-24 faster-dispatch JSON protocols/audits at design time. They stay inside the CLI's +/-0.03 m and +/-3 degree bounds and preserve the known open map, dock and r1/r3 pair plus r2 solo role assignment.
case_selection.novelty_limit: Only initial pose triples are new. Same map, seed11 spawn ordering, camera, plan and nearby pose family remain exposed. Do not call this unseen-map or broad generalization evidence. Seeds 12 and 13 shuffle to the same physical spawn ordering as seed11 and would be label-only pseudo-holdouts.

arms.controller: Frozen v26 RGB action algorithm; run in an isolated clean checkout with the exact same common flags
Revised RGB action algorithm with ACT omitted; same candidate source as candidate-act
New 128px/history4 ACT checkpoint for beam loaded motion, RGB independent stop admission; not pure ACT and not RGB final refinement

finite_first_study.execution: Run one local MuJoCo physics job at a time; no cloud, no concurrent physics load, no automatic retry. Commit/freeze candidate and baseline sources first, then run all preregistered trial IDs despite ordinary task failures while budget remains. Reserve 200 s for setup/cleanup and record any unstarted IDs explicitly if the hard aggregate limit is reached.
finite_first_study.budget_stop: A run is capped at its arm's max_wall_s. If an ACT run exceeds 1000 s or the aggregate 3600 s deadline, stop its own session cleanly, preserve timeout/error and mark remaining preregistered trials unstarted. Do not silently replace a failed arm or extend budgets. A serious source/input invariant failure pauses the cohort for audit.
finite_first_study.after_first_study: Treat this as feasibility screening. For speed/reliability qualification, preregister at least three further new pose cases and same-source repeated trials after reviewing this cohort; do not use these inspected two cases as new holdout again.

measurements.per_trial_denominator: Report planned/started/completed/physical-success/protocol-complete/timeout/launch-failure counts by arm and case. Include all ordinary failures; do not average failed run wall time into successful completion time.
measurements.primary_success: Both beam and box lifted, carried with sampled clearance, fully inside target slots, released with stable floor support for the referee tail, protocol complete; zero artificial weld steps.
measurements.contact: Record robot-robot sampled contact count, obstacle contact steps, loaded cargo floor contact samples and continuous-clearance sampling gap. Zero measured contacts is required for acceptance, with explicit sampled-only limitation.
measurements.speed: Whole mission wall_s and SIM_s, motion SIM/wall, successful paired-case wall ratio candidate-rgb/reference-rgb, stage durations including approach/fine/carry/resource wait, issued commands, expired leases and observation age. Compare successful complete pairs only and report failures beside them.
measurements.act: For every started ACT trial report ACT inference request count, response latency distribution, invalid/timeout/error count, carry entries, model stop proposals and RGB admission/rejection, premature stop, decision-budget exhaustion, attachment loss and final placement. External LLM planning call count remains a separate zero-expected field.
artifacts: new TensorBoard snapshot with failure rows

first_study_readout.action_algorithm_directional_gate: Candidate RGB must physically and procedurally succeed on both new cases with no contact/weld violation; compare its two matched successful wall times against reference v26 and require both faster plus at least 10 percent lower two-case median before describing a directional speed gain. Otherwise report exact failure and timing without a speed claim.
first_study_readout.act_feasibility_gate: Candidate ACT rgb_guarded must enter carry and finish both new cases with both cargos physically placed/released, no false model stop proposal outside RGB arrival, no contact/weld violation, and all inference requests accounted for. If it fails, keep failure as a model/controller result, including whether the shared RGB entry failed before ACT inference.
first_study_readout.interpretation_limit: Two pose cases cannot establish a reliability rate or isolate each code change. Candidate ACT versus candidate RGB measures the cost and task behavior of substituting learned loaded-beam motion under the same candidate runtime; it is not evidence that the new ACT improves over a missing old checkpoint. Successful baseline and candidate runs on different source bundles must retain exact bundle differences.
